title: feat(v4): make z.properties() a schema, and give z.instanceof() a .properties() method
body:
`z.properties(shape)` now constructs a real schema instead of an array of `z.property()` checks. It asserts the named properties in place and returns its input untouched — no new object, so prototypes, unlisted keys, and object identity survive. And because it's a schema, it finally infers. Follows up on #5912, which landed the check form; an array of checks can never narrow the type, and that was the reason to revisit it.

```ts
const httpsUrl = z.instanceof(URL).properties({
  protocol: z.literal("https:"),
  hostname: z.string().regex(z.regexes.domain),
});

type HttpsUrl = z.infer<typeof httpsUrl>;
// => URL & { protocol: "https:"; hostname: string }
```

What's in here:

- **`$ZodProperties`**, a core schema that is also a check, the way `$ZodCustom` is. As a schema it is the type gate — an object or a function, never a primitive — reports every failing key, and parses cyclic input — it returns the input identity, so the input registers as its own memo entry. It has cases in `z.compile()` (both roles), `z.toJSONSchema()` (`type: "object"` + `properties` + `required`, no `additionalProperties`; a symbol key is reported unrepresentable, as `z.object()` does), the memoizer, and `visit`.
- **The 4.5 spread still works.** The schema yields itself from `Symbol.iterator`, so `z.instanceof(URL).check(...z.properties({ ... }))` keeps compiling and running; TypeScript infers the spread element type from the iterator. The spread now reports every failing property instead of stopping at the first, since one check iterates the whole shape. One caveat: consumers on `target: es5` lose the spread form (spreading a non-array iterable requires ES2015); the schema forms work everywhere.
- **`z.instanceof()` returns a dedicated `ZodInstanceOf` class** with a `.properties()` method that narrows and chains. `z.instanceof(URL).and(z.properties({ ... }))` narrows too — intersection returns the left value when both sides come back identical.
- **As a check it asserts on whatever the base produced**, so `z.string().check(...z.properties({ length: z.number().min(3) }))` reads a string's length, exactly as `z.property()` does. The base has already typed the value there; standalone, this schema types it itself.
- **The shape is asserted and its results discarded**, exactly as `z.property()` behaves — identity can't distinguish a transform from a nested object schema rebuilding its output, so there's no cheap honest detection. Both sides therefore infer the **input** type: an output-typed inference would lie for every entry whose output differs from its input (`z.properties({ a: z.string().default("x") })` would claim `{ a: string }` and return `{}`). A plain schema has identical input and output, so the narrowing example above is unchanged.
- `z.core._properties` changes signature from `(shape)` to `(Class, shape, params?)`, matching the other schema factories. The old form shipped 12 days ago in 4.5.0.
- `when` is not settable on `z.properties()`. It gates a check inside the run loop, so it means nothing to a parsed schema, and honoring it in one role only would diverge silently.

Three axes, measured against `main` at bf990216 (gzipped bytes; retained bytes per instance over 20k instances under `--expose-gc`; parse/construction as min-of-7 fixed-count rounds):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| parse: `z.instanceof(URL).check(...z.properties({...}))` | 140 ns | 140 ns |
| construction: same schema | 7.9 µs | 9.2 µs (+16%; a real schema costs more to build than two plain check objects) |
| construction: bare `z.instanceof(URL)` | 1.32 µs | 1.34 µs |
| memory: `z.instanceof(URL)` | 2.0 KB | 2.0 KB |
| memory: `z.properties()` (2 keys) | — | 3.0 KB |
| bundle: `zod-object` / `zod-string` | 24949 / 20867 | 24977 (+28) / 20906 (+39) |
| bundle: `zod-mini-object` / `-string` / `-boolean` | 4598 / 3497 / 3021 | 4611 (+13) / 3516 (+19) / 3036 (+15) |
| bundle: instanceof + properties call site | 21470 | 21746 (+276) |

The flat +15–17 B on every bundle is the symbol-key loop added to `util.members`, which is what installs `Symbol.iterator` on the per-constructor prototype; the mini ceilings are re-measured against `main` and raised in this branch. Classic pays ~10 B more for the memoizer's shared reference predicate, which mini treeshakes. `dict-mode.ts` reports every instance `fast`.

reviews.body: Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.

> [!IMPORTANT] > The inferred output type is unsound — nothing is ever written back, so `.default()`, `.catch()` and type-changing `.transform()` inside the shape all produce values that contradict the declared type. Separately, the compiled fast path diverges from the interpreter in two ways, one of which silently returns different data inside a union. Reviewed the full diff across all 16 files, then verified each finding by running it. The design is good — `$ZodProperties` as a dual schema/check mirroring `$ZodCustom` is the right shape for this, the `Symbol.iterator` compatibility hatch is neat, and the JSON Schema `required` logic matches `objectProcessor` exactly. Suite is green (7867 passed) and the raised bundle ceilings are accurate after a build. Three things below, plus two nits inline. ### Child schemas run with an empty parse context `inst._zod.check` runs every shape child with a literal `{}` as its context. This is inherited verbatim from `$ZodCheckProperty`, so it isn't new code, but it becomes reachable at the top level for the first time now that `z.properties()` is a schema — which surfaces two behaviors: **Codecs run in the wrong direction.** The `direction: "backward"` flag lives on the context, so it's dropped: ```ts const codec = z.codec(z.string(), z.number(), { decode: Number, encode: String }); z.encode(z.object({ a: codec }), { a: 5 }); // { a: "5" } z.encode(z.properties({ a: codec }), { a: 5 }); // throws: invalid_type, expected string ``` **Cyclic input overflows the stack.** `$ZodProperties` never calls `memo?.attach(inst)`, and the fresh `{}` wouldn't carry memo state anyway, so a cycle that `z.object()` handles fine blows up: ```ts const node: any = z.lazy(() => z.properties({ next: node.optional() })); const a: any = {}; a.next = a; node.safeParse(a); // RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded ``` Worth noting the new `memoizer.ts` case does make `isRecursiveSchema()` correctly report `true` here — the detection is wired up, only the breaking isn't. Error maps and `reportInput` do still propagate, since `finalizeIssue` resolves against the outer context, so the blast radius is limited to these two. Not blocking on its own, but if `z.properties()` is going to be a first-class schema it should probably forward the context it was given.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6536?action=fix&review_id=5070383312) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6536?action=fix-approved&review_id=5070383312) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/33429351251/job/99610643161) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

Passing `ctx` through here makes backward encoding validate each discarded child in reverse, but `$ZodProperties` declares both sides from the child's input type. A type-correct encode now rejects or throws, while an `any`-cast child output can pass and be returned under the wrong declared type.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Keep property assertions forward during encode

## Affected sites
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:4981 — both schema sides intentionally use `$InferObjectInput`
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5025 — the outer backward direction reaches each child codec or transform
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5048 — the check role still validates children forward, so the two public forms diverge

## Required outcome
- `z.encode(z.properties(shape), value)` must validate the declared input-side shape and return the same value
- child traversal must retain the parse state needed for memoization and async handling without executing discarded transformations backward
- add a regression using a codec with different input/output types and a type-changing transform

## Suggested approach
- pass a context that preserves parse state but treats child traversal as a forward assertion during backward encoding; do not restore the empty context
````

</details>

`z.properties()` accepts callable values, but this gate and the memoizer wrapper only recognize `typeof value === "object"`. A recursive callable such as `fn.self = fn` therefore still overflows despite the new cycle-support contract.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Track callable reference cycles

## Affected sites
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5040 — callable inputs never register an entry
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/memoizer.ts:224 — callable inputs never take the bucket lookup path
- packages/zod/src/v4/core/memoizer.ts:287 — callable back-edges are not recognized

## Required outcome
- recursive properties schemas must terminate for both object and callable reference values accepted by `z.properties()`
- primitive behavior must remain unchanged
- add a regression with a function whose asserted property points back to itself

## Suggested approach
- use the same reference-value predicate consistently for allocation, lookup, and back-edge detection
````

</details>

This `type` rejects values the schema explicitly accepts: `z.properties({ length: z.number().min(3) }).parse("abc")` succeeds, but Ajv rejects `"abc"` against the emitted schema. Since JSON Schema `properties` cannot model arbitrary JavaScript property reads on primitives, either the runtime contract must be object-only or conversion must report this case as unrepresentable instead of emitting a narrower contract.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Primitive runtime inputs are missing from JSON Schema

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5016` — runtime rejects only `null` and `undefined`
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:384` — emitted schema accepts only JSON objects
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/properties.test.ts:16` — the primitive-input behavior is explicitly pinned

## Required outcome
- `safeParse(value).success` and validation against `toJSONSchema()` must agree for every representable input class
````

</details>

Output requiredness follows the child schema even though `z.properties()` discards the child's output: `z.properties({ a: z.string().default("x") }).parse({})` returns `{}`, while its output JSON Schema marks `a` required and Ajv rejects `{}`. The emitted property schemas and optionality need to describe the asserted input-side contract in both I/O modes, or output-changing children need to be treated as unrepresentable.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Output JSON Schema describes values that are never returned

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:390` — child processing inherits the global output mode
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:398` — output optionality uses `optout`
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:4995` — parsed child values are deliberately discarded

## Required outcome
- JSON Schema output mode must accept every value `z.properties()` can actually return, including absent defaulted properties
- Property constraints must continue to describe the values the runtime validates rather than discarded transform/default output
````

</details>

`keys` is cached separately while each schema is still read live from the caller's mutable shape. After one parse, deleting `shape.a` makes the next `safeParse()` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')`, while adding a key is silently ignored; snapshot the keys and schema references together as the previous `Object.entries()` implementation and `z.object()` do.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Shape mutation corrupts the cached parse plan

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5014` — key names are frozen on first parse
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:5023` — schema references remain live through `def.shape`
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/compile.ts:588` — compilation snapshots a different view of the same shape

## Required outcome
- A constructed schema must keep a coherent key-to-schema mapping across parses and compilation
- Mutating the object originally passed as `shape` must not cause raw runtime exceptions or compiled/interpreted drift
````

</details>
